xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The court has passed an order against DCB Bank on 26-11-2024 and the Insurance Company directing - 1. The opposite parties 3 & 4 (i.e., Insurance Company) to pay the sum assured amounts as per the master Policies of the respective loan accounts to the complainant. 2. The opposite parties 1 & 2 (i.e., DCB Bank) to cancel the memorandum of deposit of title deed and hand over the original documents to the complainant. 3. The opposite parties 1 & 2 (i.e., DCB Bank) to repay the EMI amount paid by the complainant from July 2019 (from the date of death of the borrower) till date, towards the loan availed by Late Mr. Sivagnanasundaram P. 4. The opposite parties 1 to 4, jointly and severally, to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards the deficiency of service. 5. The opposite parties 1 to 4, jointly and severally , to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/-, towards the cost of this complaint. Court has further directed to comply with the above-said direction within 2 months from the date of the receipt of the order, failing which the opposite parties 1 to 4 are liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of the realization to the Complainant.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The Court has concluded that there is deficinecy in service at the end of DCB Bank (OP No. 1 & 2) as DCB Bank furnished incorrect information of the insured person w.r.t. the membership certificate. Also the court has further conlcuded that since the policy was in the name of the deceased principal borrower, OP No. 3 & 4 i.e. insurance company have no right to repudiate the claim which amounts to unfair trade practice and deficinecy in service. DCB Bank has filed an Appeal before the state commission against the said order.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The court has passed an order against DCB Bank on 26-11-2024 and the Insurance Company directing - 1. The opposite parties 3 & 4 (i.e., Insurance Company) to pay the sum assured for the policies taken by the deceased borrower. 2. The opposite parties 1 & 2 (i.e., DCB Bank) to repay the EMI amount paid by the complainant from July 2019 (from the date of death of the borrower) till date, i.e. Rs. 18, 89,918.07, towards the loan availed by Late Mr. Sivagnanasundaram P. 3. The opposite parties 1 to 4, jointly and severally, to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards the deficiency of service. 4. The opposite parties 1 to 4, jointly and severally , to pay a sum of Rs.5,000/-, towards the cost of this complaint.
